text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 billing is concentrated on low-complexity patients across every complexity tier, but the very small records sample cannot confirm or refute whether these visits were upcoded.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is the main concern. 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with zero chronic conditions. About half of the 99215s fall on 0-1 condition patients whose sampled diagnoses are routine, such as Z09 follow-ups, unspecified abdominal pain or rash, back pain and URI (e.g., C0063401, C0063592, C0063982, C0064516). That is a pattern consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel. The documentation points the other way but is too thin to carry weight: only 5 documented 99215 claims exist, all supported at high MDM (e.g., C0063506, C0064529), and only one moderate-plus data note lacked a lab or test line. A sample this small cannot rule out cloned or templated notes. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims listed above. They should then check whether those notes show genuine high-complexity decision-making or boilerplate repeated across visits."}
